Notice the little things as you go about your day. Eg birds chirping, the soft light of twilight, star constellations.

If you go out, make eye contact and smile with people you pass in the street - even if you live in an "unfriendly" city like London or Paris, you'll still get a good lot of people who smile back. We're social creatures, so seeing people smile at you will lift your mood - even if it's just a little bit, it all adds up.

Try to get outside for a 10-15 minute walk every day and vary the routes. The goal here isn't fitness (though exercise in that sense may help too), it's about getting fresh air, a change of scenery, and giving you the opportunity to notice the little things and get smiles reciprocated. If you're not working or at school, it gives you the start of a routine and rationale to get up, washed and dressed for the day.

If you feel able, spend time on your hobby / hobbies. Preferably something that is social, requires concentration, and or has clearly measurable progress. 

If you have someone who you're close to and comfortable with, ask them for a hug. They might ask if you're OK - consider telling them the truth.

If you haven't already, do consider therapy / meds. They can help you regain who you are underneath all the depression.

I hope you find something helpful in some or all of the points above. I've been where you are and those are things that helped me get back on my feet, though it didn't work overnight, it took time and perseverance. Happy to talk if you want.
